tasks.commitBody:
The three keys the #229 census found unreferenced were never dead —
they were written for surfaces that had not been finished. They now
reach their screens.

A completed visibility repair announces itself: the page gains a
persistent role=status live region in the house idiom
(event-create-status, roster-reorder-status — imperative text on a
plain state string, cleared when the next attempt starts, no
timer), carrying profile_repair_done. The banner's unmount stays as
it was; what changes is that a screen reader — and anyone — now
hears that a change to who can see their personal data actually
landed. Failures keep today's error banner, so success and failure
read differently.

The per-field visibility picker gains its missing title and
operating instruction: a real h2 (profile_visibility_title) above
the field list with profile_visibility_intro as its explanatory
line — the one-level-per-field rule and tap-to-move instruction,
already written and translated, finally shown. profile_intro stays
as the page's own introduction.

Riding along per the #260 review note: refreshCompletionGate's
rejection handler now distinguishes stale from live — a stale
rejection stays silent (the race fix), a live failure to resolve
membership standing reaches console.error like every other failure
in this file. No user-visible change; an hour of future pilot
debugging bought for three lines.

Live gate (Mihkel): on /profile, move a field's visibility and
complete the repair — a confirmation appears (and is announced);
the field list now has its title and instruction above it, in all
four languages.
